cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a carved argillite amulet in the form of a stylized fish/marine creature with formline details and haliotis shell inlay, a well-documented Haida art form (argillite carving with abalone inlay is highly characteristic of Haida material culture).

physical.title: amulet
physical.summary: Small carving, an amulet (?), made from a piece of soft grey stone, possibly argillite, in the form a marine/water creature, probably a salmon, carved in a rough ovoid, with formline details. The hooked mouth and gills are incised as are the ventral fins, the dorsal fin being very slight; the tail, carved with a face, points downards, acting as a platform for a small bear-like creature situated under the belly of the fish with the head touching the ventral fins. The amulet is inlaid with haliotis, four rectangular pieces along the body of the fish, one of the pieces missing; the eyes and ventral fins of the fish are also inlaid, as were once the eyes of the face on the tail. The dorsal fin is pierced with a hole for suspension, a short length of skin thong remaining. The whole item shows great wear and age.
